title: Cosanima license migration: MIT → Apache-2.0
goal: Migrate cosanima (core crate, distribution artifacts, and the six frontend repos) from MIT to Apache-2.0 before opening to contributors, coupling a contributor-agreement decision to the change.

title: Core repo license → Apache-2.0
body: Replace the MIT LICENSE file (currently the MIT text at the repo root) with the Apache-2.0 text and set Cargo.toml `license = "Apache-2.0"` (currently "MIT", Cargo.toml line 6). Keep the copyright line (John Le Drew) in the NOTICE-style attribution per Apache-2.0 §4.

title: Distribution license sweep
body: Distribution sweep: all seven brew formulae (scanner.rb + apg-cpp/csharp/go/java/rust/ts.rb, each currently `license "MIT"`) change to `license "Apache-2.0"`; README license badge/mentions and install.sh headers reflect Apache-2.0.

title: Frontend repos inherit Apache-2.0
body: Post-split, each of the six frontend repos (cosanima-go/java/cpp/rust/ts/csharp) ships the identical Apache-2.0 LICENSE text at its v1.0.0 tag, so all seven repos carry one license on the 1.0 flag-day.

summary: Migrate MIT → Apache-2.0 (source 'Leaning Apache-2.0' treated as decided per the binding design conversation): explicit patent grant + contributor protection clause matter before opening to contributors.

body: No change to third-party/vendored dependencies' own licenses (e.g. the C++ tree-sitter vendors stay MIT); only the project's own LICENSE text and metadata change.
No retroactive relicense of already-shipped apg 0.x releases; the MIT→Apache-2.0 change applies at the 1.0.0 cut.

No contributor-onboarding / PR-check CI automation pre-1.0; the contributor agreement form is decided but its operational rollout (PR-level CI, onboarding docs) is deferred to post-1.0 behind this decision.
Cargo.toml `license = "Apache-2.0"` and the repo-root LICENSE file contain the full Apache-2.0 text with the copyright attribution.
No project-owned file declares MIT: a `rg` sweep for MIT/`license "MIT"` over Cargo.toml, README, install.sh, and Formula/*.rb returns no project-owned MIT declarations.
All seven repos (core + six frontends) carry the identical Apache-2.0 LICENSE at their v1.0.0 tags.
`brew audit` on the renamed formulae passes the license field, and `cargo metadata` reports the Apache-2.0 license.
Vendored third-party files retain their own license headers (tree-sitter etc. unchanged by the sweep).

summary: Contributor agreement — DECIDED NOW, binding for 1.0: DCO (Developer Certificate of Origin) sign-off is the contribution mechanism for 1.0, complementing Apache-2.0's patent grant. Not deferred: the DCO decision is binding at the 1.0 flag-day; only its operational rollout (PR-level CI, onboarding docs) lands post-1.0 [with user].

body: source: SPEC-1.0.0.md 'Leaning Apache-2.0 (from MIT)' was an open leaning and the contributor-agreement form was explicitly an undecided 'own decision' coupled to Apache-2.0; materialized as decided: Apache-2.0 is binding for 1.0. The contributor agreement is DCO (Developer Certificate of Origin) sign-off, binding for 1.0 (decided now, per the user's ruling — supersedes the earlier DCO-leaning-deferred wording) [with user].

source/ruling: the user ruled that DCO (Developer Certificate of Origin) sign-off is the binding contribution mechanism for 1.0 — DECIDED NOW, not deferred to post-1.0 onboarding. inconsistency: Decision D2 (and note-1) previously ruled DCO 'deferred to post-1.0 onboarding' [autonomous]. resolution: D2 now states DCO sign-off is binding for 1.0 (decided, complementing Apache-2.0's patent grant); only the operational rollout (PR-level CI, onboarding docs) is deferred; note-1 updated to remove the 'deferred' wording [with user].
